title: First derivative — increasing or decreasing
goal: Find where a graph climbs uphill ($f'(x) > 0$) and where it slides downhill ($f'(x) < 0$) by testing the sign of its first derivative.

beforeThis.skill: Quick check: a function can only switch from uphill to downhill at places where $f'(x) = 0$ (flat spots) or where $f(x)$ or $f'(x)$ is undefined.

questions.asking: Match each of the five graphed curves $A(x)$ through $E(x)$ to its derivative formula from $l(x), m(x), n(x), o(x), p(x)$ by comparing where each curve rises, falls, and levels off at $x = \pm 2$.
questions.statement:
Match each function graphed below to its derivative from the list. (For example, which function on the list corresponds to $A'(x)$?)

The $y$-axes have been scaled to make the curve’s behaviour clear, so the vertical scales differ from graph to graph.

$$l(x) = (x - 2)^4 \qquad m(x) = (x - 2)^4(x + 2) \qquad n(x) = (x - 2)^2(x + 2)^2$$$$o(x) = (x - 2)(x + 2)^3 \qquad p(x) = (x + 2)^4$$

figures.alt: Three graphs with ticks at x = -2 and x = 2: green curve y = A(x) increases everywhere with a flat horizontal terrace at x = 2; blue curve y = B(x) increases everywhere with a flat horizontal terrace at x = -2; red curve y = C(x) increases everywhere with flat horizontal terraces at both x = -2 and x = 2.

Two graphs with ticks at x = -2 and x = 2: orange curve y = D(x) rises to a peak at x = -2 (with a terrace there), falls to a minimum at x = 2, and rises for x > 2; magenta curve y = E(x) falls to a minimum at x = -2, then rises for x > -2 with a flat horizontal terrace at x = 2.
